findings.problem: A matter of the rule, not of the code, and for the lead before the pre-registration is committed. On real stock Stage 1 walks the own-swing reading, exactly as C3 defines it, is well below Stage 1's reading of the same low points, and it fails the open-loop row on walks that Stage 1 passes. The cause is where the 2 % load rule puts the ends of a foot's own swing: the lift-off coincides with the reference's, but the touchdown comes later, so the middle half sits later than the foot's height profile and its 75 % edge lies on the steep falling flank. The design's test row models the simulated foot as the reference purely delayed, which is the one case where this does not show. V0's planned reading at 0.40 m/s is 0.5 x 0.081 H = 0.0405 H, 0.25 mm above the 0.04 H limit, so the term is likely to fail for the control in most episodes, and perhaps for the candidate (planned 0.0475 H); that last sentence is my extrapolation, not a measurement.
findings.evidence: Stock conditions walk/nominal, walk/brisk, walk/fr05 of 75-M-H-10, seeds 3042-3044, hard floor, no servo delay, last 10 s, read on the live recorder (real_table.py, logs/real_table.log). Row R2/42, own-swing against Stage 1's: nominal 0.0436, 0.0428, 0.0445 H against 0.0475, 0.0473, 0.0481 H; brisk 0.0433, 0.0436, 0.0455 against 0.0541, 0.0533, 0.0535; fr05 0.0407, 0.0418, 0.0417 against 0.0541, 0.0537, 0.0548 (term true in all nine, smallest margin 0.3 mm). Row R0: nominal 0.0334, 0.0330, 0.0335 H and brisk 0.0359, 0.0356, 0.0377 H, term false in six of six, where Stage 1 reads 0.0476-0.0538 H. Half the planned lift is 0.0500 H (nominal) and 0.0550 H (brisk, fr05). Brisk, seed 3042 (logs/real_swing_detail.log and the timing run): own lift-off minus the reference's, median +1.5 ms (R2/42) and -1.6 ms (R0); own touchdown minus the reference's, median +7.0 ms (R2/42) and +17.4 ms (R0); the foot's lowest point is within 1 mm of the floor for a median 20 ms at the start and 28 ms at the end of the own swing; the height peak is at 48.4 % of the own duration; the 75 % edge is the minimum in 23 of 23 swings, on a flank of -0.475 m/s. The same low points read on the reference's clock with interpolated edges give 0.0527 H (R2/42) and 0.0526 H (R0). The touchdown is the first raw contact (the debounce moved none of them). readings.py equals my own implementation of the rule text bit for bit on these episodes (0.021742895698668063 m and 0.018033855310931126 m), so the code is not the cause.
findings.fix: No change to the reading's code. The lead decides before PREREG_75 is committed, and the choice is his: either keep C3 as written and add an expectation sentence with these numbers, as C2 does for the tail servo (including that the R0 row fails the term on Stage 1's own nominal and brisk walks); or change the definition of the swing's ends or of its middle half in C3 and in 3.8 (a) before any reference is frozen. In either case: add one sentence to readings.py's docstring (a) saying that the own swing's ends are the 2 % load crossings and that on stock walks the touchdown comes 7-17 ms after the reference's; have WP B's reread record, per episode, the own swing's duration, the reference swing's duration and which edge gave the minimum; and say in design 4.4 that row 1 tests a pure delay only.

findings.problem: Five readings of the rule's text are chosen in the code and stated only in docstrings; the pre-registered text does not carry them. (1) "No reference swing in the window is interrupted" is read as reference swings wholly inside the window, so a stub in a reference swing that the window's start cuts is not flagged, though its second part is still read. (2) With W = [t_c, ...] in the turn item, the first swing after the command is read only if the foot's 2 % load lift-off is not before t_c; otherwise it is cut and the "less one" allowance absorbs it. (3) A cut swing counts toward its reference swing's interruption. (4) With no stopped time, touchdowns are counted to the trace's end. (5) C7 calls the stopped time "decision 18's quantity", but the bar reads speed along the commanded heading from an interpolated command instant, while decision 18 uses the trunk's heading at the first update past the command.
findings.evidence: (1) My trace with a 30 ms stub and the window starting 40 ms into that reference swing: interrupted 0, second part read at 5.04 mm. (2) Own lift-off 4 ms before the reference's and the window starting 2 ms before it: class swing_cut, own [9, 9] against ref [10, 9], term true; on the stock episodes the own lift-off came -4.9 to +5.8 ms from the reference's. (5) Stock start-and-stop episode, R2/42, seed 3042: the bar's reading is 0.687 s = 0.635 strides, decision 18's is 0.573 strides, and stop_reading returns 0.5733 when given Stage 1's instant and the trunk's heading (-1.57 degrees from the commanded one), so the gap is the definition's.
findings.fix: The lead adds to PREREG C3: "a reference swing is in the window when every one of its updates is; a swing that the window cuts is not read but counts for its reference swing; air gaps are counted when wholly inside", and decides whether the turn's first swing must be read (for instance by counting swings from a stated time before t_c) or accepts point (2) in words. To C7: "if the speed never settles the count runs to the end of the trace" and "along the commanded heading (decision 18's own reading, along the trunk's heading at the command, is recorded beside it)".

findings.problem: A low point that is not finite is handled by accident. Python's min() drops a NaN that is not its first argument and returns NaN when it is. So a NaN at an update strictly between the edges is silently ignored, a NaN next to an edge makes that swing's reading NaN, and min(readings) over the swings then depends on their order. ref_swing is checked for finiteness at line 178; low is not.
findings.evidence: One 40 mm swing: NaN at an interior update of the middle half reads 0.0200018 m, the same as the clean trace; NaN at the update just before or just after the 25 % edge reads nan. Two swings, the first with a NaN edge and the second at 5 mm: the result is nan.
findings.fix: After line 207 take the two edge values into variables and raise ValueError("low is not finite inside a read swing") unless both and every value of `between` are finite.

findings.problem: line_reading returns complete=True whenever two updates fall in [ta, tb], even if the trace does not span the window. c(tb) is then np.interp's clamp to the last update, so `along` is a shorter walk's distance presented as the window's. turn_reading has window_reached for the same case; line_reading has nothing the caller can use for rule C8.
findings.evidence: A trace ending at 8.99 s read over [5.99, 15.99]: complete True, along 1.26 m (logs/traces_line_turn_stop.log).
findings.fix: Add window_reached = bool(t[0] <= ta + EPS_S and t[-1] >= tb - EPS_S) to the returned dict, and document that the caller treats a false value on an episode that did not fall as an error.

findings.problem: The docstring says a trace can be read again with these functions, and the design's trace holds t100 and low100 as float32. Every time comparison uses 1e-9 s of slack, far below float32 resolution at a few seconds, so a re-read from float32 times is not the live reading: updates that sit exactly on a lift-off, a touchdown or a window edge can change sides.
findings.evidence: 30 synthetic walks of 40 s read live and again with t_u and low passed through float32: the reading moved by up to 6.0e-7 m; with low alone in float32, 6.3e-10 m. The counts happened to be equal in these 30; an update at 25.6 s becomes 25.600000381 s.
findings.fix: State in the docstring that t_u must be the recorder's float64 times, or times rebuilt as k x 5 x dt; and tell WP B to store t100 as float64 or not at all (rebuild it from dt and the row count) so that `bar reread` gives the live numbers.

findings.problem: The reference's own readings assume the file's first frame is at t = 0. reference_heading_at interpolates at rate x tau_s of the file's absolute time, and forward_stopped_s, touchdown_s and time_to_80deg_bar_s are absolute file times, while the docstring says "bar time since the command, which is the file's first frame". A file whose t starts elsewhere would be read at the wrong place without an error.
findings.evidence: Code reading; every Stage 1 transition file I opened starts at t[0] = 0.0, so nothing is wrong today.
findings.fix: Use t0 = t[0]: np.interp(t0 + rate * tau_s, t, h) at line 429; subtract t0 from t_stop and the touchdown times at 483-491 and from the interpolated time at 511. Or raise ValueError when abs(t[0]) > 1e-12.

findings.problem: canonical differs from the design's frozen listing (json.dumps(..., allow_nan=False) on the plain value). A float that is not finite is hashed as the string "NaN", "Infinity" or "-Infinity", so a NaN and the string "NaN" hash alike; and write_json writes bare NaN tokens, which is Stage 1's layout but not strict JSON. The change is needed: a stand's period and duty are NaN in gaits.b, which is in MOVE_SUBSET, so the listed form would raise on every start and stop entry. But it is a silent change to a listed behaviour, and any package or reviewer that re-hashes an entry with plain json.dumps gets another hash or an error.
findings.evidence: s2io.canonical([nan, inf, -inf]) is b'["NaN","Infinity","-Infinity"]' (the builder's own test line 121); Stage 1's transitions.json has gaits.b.period NaN for stop and start.
findings.fix: No code change. The builder reports it; the lead amends design 2.1's canonical line to say so, and the briefs of the set, bar and regression packages say that entry and key hashes go through s2io.sha256_json only.

verdict: Work package R's code does what the rules say, and I found no blocker in it; the one thing that needs a decision is the toe-clearance rule itself, before the pre-registration is committed. readings.py agrees with a second implementation I wrote from the rule text alone on 1,500 random traces for each of the own-swing, stop, line and turn readings, and bit for bit on real stock episodes; contact, the drive ratios and the walk's along and lateral values equal Stage 1's to the last digit on a live recorder. The six traces asked for read as the rules say: a 10 ms delay leaves the own-swing reading where it was; a touchdown at 48 % is a swing and fails on its own middle half; a mid-swing stub is an interrupted swing; 0.26 m of drift fails the line; 79 degrees fails and 81 passes; a third touchdown fails the stop. s2io and setio hold up (atomic writes, locks, exact names, ignore rules, planned swings equal to a fine sampling of four real tracks). Two findings are major. First, on stock Stage 1 walks the own-swing reading as C3 defines it is 0.004 to 0.013 H below Stage 1's for R2/42 and fails R0 on its own nominal and brisk walks in six of six episodes, because the 2 % load touchdown comes 7 to 17 ms after the reference's; V0's planned reading at 0.40 m/s is only 0.25 mm above the limit. Second, 17 of 65 wrong-rule changes to readings.py pass the builder's tests; 14 added tests, written and checked, catch all of them. The rest are minor. I ran no delayed row, no Stage 2 set and no real 90 degree turn or causal stop, since none exists in this worktree yet.
